definitions: To turn from one side to the other, or from the back to the front, or vice versa.
To transfer or carry forward an amount or balance from one period to the next.
To submit or yield to someone's demands or pressure.
To renew a loan or agreement instead of paying it off.
examples: The dog loves to roll over for a belly rub.
We decided to roll over the remaining vacation days to next year.
The company had to roll over and accept the union's terms.
They will roll over the existing contract for another six months.
